The cause is in `src/leaks.py`, line 8:

```python
text = json.dumps(actions).lower()
```

`json.dumps` escapes every backslash in the transcript, so `C:\Users\dana` is stored in the serialized text as `c:\\users\\dana`. The check then looks for the secret `C:\Users\dana` as a plain substring of that text. The single-backslash secret never matches the doubled-backslash text, so the transcript passes. A `/home/dana` secret has no backslashes, so it survives serialization unchanged and is caught.

I reproduced this by running the function directly:

- Transcript containing `type C:\Users\dana\notes.txt`, secret `C:\Users\dana`: returns `[]` (leak missed)
- Transcript containing `cat /home/dana/notes.txt`, secret `/home/dana`: returns `['/home/dana']` (caught)

The test file doesn't cover this. `tests/test_leaks.py` only tests POSIX-style home paths, so the gap went unnoticed.

The fix belongs to the other session, so I made no changes. The likely direction is to compare the secret against the raw text of the transcript, or to also check the secret's JSON-escaped form, rather than the escaped whole-document string. A test with a Windows path would catch the regression.
